summary: The paper proposes SteerVAD, which identifies a small set of attention heads in a frozen InternVL3 model and applies context-conditioned feature scaling via a lightweight controller for video anomaly detection. The direction is interesting, and the reported results on UCF-Crime and XD-Violence, together with several ablations, suggest that targeted internal intervention may be useful. However, the supervision protocol for the 1% calibration data is not specified clearly enough, the gains over the strongest baselines are reported without uncertainty estimates, and some claims about "tuning-free," "real-time," and manifold rectification are stronger than the evidence. As submitted, this feels promising but not yet at the confidence level I would want for ICLR acceptance.
strengths: The core idea of intervening on internal frozen-MLLM representations for VAD, rather than only prompting or fully fine-tuning, is interesting and potentially impactful.
The method is lightweight in terms of trainable components, and the RSA plus hierarchical controller design is conceptually simple enough to be practically appealing.
The experiments include useful ablations on controller components, expert selection, calibration size, and key hyperparameters, which gives some visibility into why the method works.

key_concerns.issue: The supervision protocol for the calibration set is unclear: RSA and the BCE objective require fine-grained normal/anomalous labels at the segment level, but UCF-Crime and XD-Violence are typically used with weak video-level supervision during training, so it is hard to interpret the actual annotation cost and fairness of the comparison.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: State exactly what labels are used on the 1% subset, whether any additional temporal annotation was introduced, and compare against baselines under the same supervision budget; if only video-level labels are used, revise the objective and evaluation protocol accordingly.

key_concerns.issue: The claimed SOTA gains over the strongest baselines are relatively small, but the main comparison table provides no multi-seed variance, confidence intervals, or significance tests, so it is unclear whether the reported improvements are statistically reliable.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Report mean and standard deviation over multiple random 1% calibration subsets and training seeds on both datasets, include significance testing against the strongest prior methods, and ideally rerun close baselines under the same calibration budget.

key_concerns.issue: The paper claims real-time single-pass detection, yet the Gaussian smoothing in Eq. (6) appears non-causal and may use future frames; similarly, the manifold-rectification claim is supported mainly by t-SNE/UMAP visualizations rather than quantitative geometry analyses.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Either evaluate a causal online variant or soften the real-time claim, and add quantitative before/after measures of separability or geometry that do not rely only on 2D embedding plots.

key_concerns.issue: Model-selection and generality evidence are limited: LAE discovery and controller training use the same tiny subset, the validation protocol for K, F, sigma_g, and lambda_reg is not described, and experiments are limited to one backbone on two datasets.
key_concerns.suggested_fix: Use a held-out validation or nested calibration split, describe the hyperparameter selection procedure explicitly, and add at least one additional backbone or transfer setting to support broader claims.

questions_for_authors: What exact supervision granularity is used in D_calib, and how are anomalous versus normal segments labeled for RSA and the BCE loss on UCF-Crime and XD-Violence?

How exactly are LAE features extracted from InternVL3: which token positions are used, whether features are taken pre- or post-attention/output projection, how temporal pooling is done, and what prompt/template is used during inference?
How were K, F, sigma_g, lambda_reg, and any other tuning choices selected without test leakage, and was there a separate validation split inside the 1% calibration set?
Can you provide multi-seed, multi-subset results with confidence intervals and significance tests versus HiProbeVAD and VERA on both datasets?
calibration_check: Only partially: the benchmark results are plausible, but the broader claims about tuning-free real-time manifold rectification are stronger than the evidence and protocol description currently support.

significance.justification: Adapting frozen multimodal models for VAD is a relevant problem, but the impact of this paper depends on stronger validation of the claimed gains.

novelty.justification: Selecting task-aligned attention heads and applying context-conditioned feature scaling inside a frozen MLLM is moderately original, although the components are built from familiar ideas in probing and lightweight adaptation.

rigor.justification: The method is plausible and includes reasonable ablations, but unclear supervision details and an online-evaluation mismatch reduce confidence in the soundness of the claims.

statistical_soundness.justification: Main benchmark results lack confidence intervals, significance tests, and seed variability despite small margins over the strongest baselines.

calibration_honesty.justification: Several claims, especially around tuning-free operation, real-time detection, and manifold rectification, are stated more strongly than the presented evidence warrants.

clarity.justification: The overall narrative is readable and the method is organized clearly, but important implementation and protocol details are underspecified.

structure_compliance.justification: The submission follows a standard conference-paper structure with appropriate sections and a coherent experimental story.

reproducibility.justification: Many hyperparameters are reported, but the feature-extraction pipeline, prompting details, label construction, and model-selection protocol are not specified well enough for confident reproduction.

related_work.justification: The paper covers major VAD and MLLM directions reasonably well, though the distinction from adjacent lightweight adaptation or intervention methods could be sharper.

figure_quality.justification: From the captions, the figures and tables appear informative and well aligned with the main claims, especially the framework diagram and ablation tables.

breadth_generality.justification: Evidence is limited to two datasets and a single backbone, which is not enough to support broad claims about the generality of the intervention paradigm.

overall_recommendation.justification: This is a promising borderline-reject submission: the idea is interesting, but the current evidence and protocol clarity fall short of the ICLR acceptance bar.
